title: Extension of Home Improvement Programme to Flats Built after 1986
what_it_is: Extension of Home Improvement Programme to Flats Built after 1986

sections.label: HIP eligibility and extension
sections.summary: Flats built up to 1986 without the Main Upgrading Programme are eligible for HIP, with over 200,000 flats announced and selection of remaining eligible flats to be completed by FY2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Flats built up to 1986 and which have not undergone the Main Upgrading Programme are eligible for HIP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To date, HIP has been announced for over 200,000 flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Housing and Development Board (HDB) is working to first complete the selection of the remaining flats eligible for HIP by financial years (FY) 2018 before we assess whether to extend HIP beyond the current cohort of flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But as with all publicly-funded programmes, this will be contingent on the Government's fiscal position and budget availability.

sections.label: Upgrading cost sustainability
sections.summary: The last HIP announced in 2007 will only be completed in FY2018, and the Government must consider sustainability and affordability for another multi-year upgrading round.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As I have mentioned, it is not a small expense because an upgrading project is not just a one-time expenditure; it is a multi-year expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The last upgrading HIP was announced in 2007, and we are only going to be able to complete it in FY2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: More than 10 years, billions of dollars being invested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: When we want to think about another round of upgrading, I think it is fair and prudent for the Government to think about sustainability, to consider whether or not we are able to afford such a major programme that will run through many years, potentially even past this term and future terms of Government.
